summary: The framing correctly separates a finite support reduction, a paper proof of the stronger support bound, and a near-extremal completion argument from any actual exclusion of the rank-four obstruction. The explicit distinct-member and empty-core conventions avoid two common sunflower ambiguities. The reflexive intersection convention also makes the rank-zero endpoint coherent. I verified the general inequality's stated interface and elementary counting argument; I have not yet certified the complete support-56 or nine-triple arguments in this framing round. The manuscript's distinction between local unresolved Lean inputs and a previously reported computational extremal result is mathematically appropriate, subject to the scheduled source audit.

The prose accurately reflects this interface. A singleton family containing the empty set fails reflexive intersection, so rank zero forces the empty family.
